name: Barnyard Millet
description: Barnyard millet (Echinochloa frumentacea) is a nutritious, gluten-free grain with high fiber, protein, and iron. Perfect for diabetes management and digestive health.
howToUse: Cook 1:3 ratio (1 cup millet : 3 cups water). Use in porridges, upma, dosa, idli, or as rice substitute.

name: Browntop Millet
description: Browntop millet is rich in antioxidants, dietary fiber, and minerals. Excellent for weight loss, heart health, and as a sustainable supergrain.
howToUse: 1:2.5 ratio cooking. Ideal for salads, pulao, khichdi, or fermented dosa batter.

name: Finger Millet (Ragi)
description: Ragi is a powerhouse of calcium, iron, and amino acids. Famous for bone health, lactation support, and diabetes control.
howToUse: 1:3 ratio. Ragi mudde, dosa, roti, malt, porridge, or fermented drinks.

name: Foxtail Millet
description: Foxtail millet is protein-rich with low carbs, perfect for PCOS, thyroid issues, and sustained energy.
howToUse: 1:2 ratio. Pongal, upma, biryani, lemonade, or sweet pongal.

name: Jowar (Sorghum)
description: Jowar is weight-loss friendly, high in protein and fiber, gluten-free alternative to wheat.
howToUse: 1:3 ratio. Bhakri, roti, upma, khichdi, or porridge.

name: Kodo Millet
description: Kodo millet is the highest in antioxidants among millets, excellent for skin health and anti-aging.
howToUse: 1:3 ratio. Dosa, idli, upma, payasam, or as rice substitute.

name: Little Millet
description: Easy-to-digest millet with high fiber and minerals. Perfect for all ages including kids and seniors.
howToUse: 1:2.5 ratio. Khichdi, pongal, pulao, or daily rice replacement.

name: Pearl Millet (Bajra)
description: Iron-rich bajra strengthens immunity, hemoglobin levels, and is winter superfood.
howToUse: 1:3 ratio. Roti, khichdi, porridge, or stuffed paratha.

name: Brown Millet
description: Nutrient-dense brown millet packed with vitamins, minerals, and fiber for overall wellness.
howToUse: 1:3 ratio. Versatile for all Indian dishes - rice, roti, porridge.
